title: Presheaf test for a Yoneda colimit relation
statement:
Use the universes and local smallness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and the spaces, coherent functors, transformations, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $C$ be a small quasicategory, let $\mathcal S$ be the infinity category of small spaces, and let $\mathcal P(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, with Yoneda $y(c)=\operatorname{Map}_C(-,c)$. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set and $\lambda:p\to\Delta_Ka$ any coherent cocone in $C$, not necessarily colimiting. The presheaf colimit exists; put $B_\lambda=\operatorname{colim}_K(yp)$ and let $s_\lambda:B_\lambda\to y(a)$ be induced by $y\lambda$. For every $X\in\mathcal P(C)$ there are equivalences of spaces, natural coherently in $X$ and the cocone,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(y(a),X)\simeq X(a),\qquad \operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(B_\lambda,X)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(p(k)).$$
Under these equivalences precomposition with $s_\lambda$ is the comparison map $X(a)\to\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(p(k))$ whose components are $X(\lambda_k)$ and whose coherences are supplied by $X\lambda$. In particular $X$ is local for $s_\lambda$, meaning that this precomposition map is an equivalence, if and only if that comparison is an equivalence. The empty base is included and its limit is terminal. For $X=y(c)$, if $\lambda$ is colimiting in $C$, this comparison is an equivalence.

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.3.6.2, proof of (3), printed pp. 414-415, the mapping-space test for the relation s_alpha; Proposition 5.1.3.1 (Yoneda) and the colimit mapping-space criterion identify the actual comparison, including its coherences. Agent-formulated auxiliary consequence; read the April 9, 2017 HTT text online. Not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical assertion.

proof.text: The presheaf infinity-category $\mathcal P(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ admits all small colimits by the free-cocompletion theorem for a small infinity category. Therefore the coherent diagram $y\circ p$ has a colimit cocone with apex $B_\lambda$, and the coherent cocone $y\lambda:y\circ p\to\Delta_Ky(a)$ induces a map $s_\lambda:B_\lambda\to y(a)$ by the universal property of that colimit.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.4 (presheaf colimits), and Proposition 5.3.6.2 proof of (3), printed pp. 414–415 (the induced relation map)

proof.text: Apply the Yoneda evaluation equivalence in the presheaf category to the object $a$. For every $X\in\mathcal P(C)$, evaluation at $\operatorname{id}_a$ gives the natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(y(a),X)\simeq X(a)$, including its coherent dependence on $X$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.2, pp. 324–325, in the representable-presheaf variance used here

proof.text: Use the dual colimiting-cocone mapping-space criterion in the Yoneda limits lemma with $\mathcal E=\mathcal P(C)$, diagram $y\circ p$, and its colimit cocone. It gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(B_\lambda,X)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(y(p(k)),X)$. The equivalences are natural in the diagram, cocone, and testing object. Substituting the Yoneda evaluation equivalence at each $p(k)$ identifies the right side with $\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(p(k))$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.2.2 and Corollary 5.1.2.3, together with the opposite/cocone form of Propositions 5.1.3.1–5.1.3.2

proof.text: Write $\iota:yp\to\Delta_K B_\lambda$ for the colimit cocone. By the defining universal property of $s_\lambda$, the coherent composite $s_\lambda\iota$ is $y\lambda$, with its specified higher homotopies. Under step 3, precomposition by $s_\lambda$ therefore sends a coherent map $f:y(a)\to X$ to the whole compatible family $f\circ y\lambda$. Let $\eta_{b,X}:\operatorname{Map}(y(b),X)\simeq X(b)$ be the natural equivalence of step 2. Its naturality on $\lambda_k:p(k)\to a$ gives $\eta_{p(k),X}(f\circ y(\lambda_k))=X(\lambda_k)(\eta_{a,X}(f))$ up to its specified homotopy. This is an equality of coherent cones, rather than only components: naturality of $\eta$ on $C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal P(C)$ applies to every simplex of $\lambda$, and the mapping-space comparison in step 3 is natural in the diagram. Thus the resulting map is the comparison induced by $X\lambda$, coherently in $X$ and the cocone. Conjugating a map by equivalences preserves and reflects being an equivalence, proving the locality assertion.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.2, proof of (3), pp. 414–415, with the Yoneda and colimit mapping-space naturality from Propositions 5.1.2.2–5.1.3.2

proof.text: For $X=y(c)$ and a colimiting cocone $\lambda$ in $C$, the dual colimiting-cocone mapping-space criterion in $C$ gives $\operatorname{Map}_C(a,c)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_C(p(k),c)$. Its map is induced by the original cocone $\lambda$, so it is exactly the comparison $X(a)\to\lim Xp$ identified in step 4. For $K=\varnothing$, step 1 makes $B_\lambda$ an initial presheaf and step 3 identifies $\operatorname{Map}(B_\lambda,X)$ with the terminal space; for arbitrary apex $a$ the comparison is simply $X(a)\to *$. Only when this empty cocone is colimiting in $C$ must $a$ itself be initial, and then the same mapping-space criterion gives $\operatorname{Map}_C(a,c)\simeq *$.

source.place: Propositions 5.1.2.2–5.1.3.2, including the colimiting-cocone criterion and its empty-diagram case
